newsitem.title: ITALY: Mediaset buys Fininvest's Spanish TV stakes.
newsitem.headline: Mediaset buys Fininvest's Spanish TV stakes.

text.p: Italian television and advertising group Mediaset said it had exercised options to buy stakes in three Spanish television companies from its parent company Fininvest.

A Mediaset statement said its board meeting had approved the exercise of options granted in July to buy 25 percent stakes each in Gestevision Telecinco SA, Publiespana SA and Estudios Telecinco SA from Fininvest for a total of 15.979 billion pesetas.

The value of the three stakes was assessed by three investment banks IMI, Lehman Brothers and Morgan Stanley, and the price paid by Mediaset was fixed at 20 percent below the valuation price, amounting to some 3.995 billion pesetas below the valuation.
The statement said that Mediaset will decide at its next board meeting in January over the exercise of an option to buy a 10 percent stake in Italian pay-TV group Telepiu, again from Fininvest.

Mediaset has also decided to acquire the Spanish language television rights for 5,000 films from the three companies for $26.8 million, at a discount of $6.7 million from a valuation made by Kagan World Media.
After the flotation of Mediaset on the Milan bourse in the summer, former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi's Fininvest company controls around 50 percent of the company.
